lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.unitTitle: Caring for Home and Shared Spaces
lessonRef.title: Mastery check: task sizing

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can practice task sizing. I will do one step at a time and check one result.
scenario: The learner is handed (or writes) a list of five household tasks that range from very small (put away three books) to large (reorganize a closet), and must judge, without adult help, which ones can be done in one sitting and which need to be split into smaller steps.
safetyNotes: This is a planning task; no physical task execution is required for scoring.
materials: adult-or-local: a real or provided list of five household tasks

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u01-l05-model-card. Watch one complete example.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u01-l05-guided-card. Do the coached move.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u01-l05-independent-card. Choose one complete route. Follow its steps.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g5-u01-l05-evidence-record. Save one result and one reflection.

prompts.text: Rate how confident you are in your own task-sizing judgment right now (very / somewhat / not yet). Cite one specific task from your list as evidence for that rating, and choose: ready to try a bigger task on your own, ready to review this again later, or need a different explanation of task sizing.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g5-u01-l05-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g5-u01-l05-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g5-u01-l05-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Sorting accuracy: Correctly separates true one-sitting tasks from multi-step ones. | First-step sizing: First step is specific and completable in under ten minutes. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g5-u01-l05-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Give the learner one new, larger task they haven't sized before and have them break it into a full sequence of right-sized steps, not just the first one.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can practice task sizing. I will do one step at a time and check one result.

duration.sessionPattern: 5 minutes model, 5–7 minutes guided try, 10–15 minutes learner task, 5 minutes evidence and retry check
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

localMaterials.label: paper and pencil
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

localMaterials.label: a real or provided list of five household tasks
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

materials.noPurchaseRule: No purchase is required. Use the complete fictional route when a local material, setting, source, or adult is unavailable.

resources.title: task sizing worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner is handed (or writes) a list of five household tasks that range from very small (put away three books) to large (reorganize a closet), and must judge, without adult help, which ones can be done in one sitting and which need to be split into smaller steps.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact task sizing decision or action.
Model move 2: Quickly recall: what's one task you tried to do all at once recently that turned out to be too big?
Model move 3: Sort your five tasks into 'one sitting' and 'needs steps.' For every task in the 'needs steps' pile, write a first step that is genuinely small enough to finish in under ten minutes.
Model check: Sorting accuracy: Correctly separates true one-sitting tasks from multi-step ones. | First-step sizing: First step is specific and completable in under ten minutes.

resources.title: task sizing action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal for task sizing.
2. Watch the worked move on swk-rfl-g5-u01-l05-model-card.
3. Do one coached move on swk-rfl-g5-u01-l05-guided-card.
4. Complete the chosen route on swk-rfl-g5-u01-l05-independent-card.
5. Save the small record on swk-rfl-g5-u01-l05-evidence-record; use swk-rfl-g5-u01-l05-retry-pair if a step is missed.

resources.title: task sizing coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner is handed (or writes) a list of five household tasks that range from very small (put away three books) to large (reorganize a closet), and must judge, without adult help, which ones can be done in one sitting and which need to be split into smaller steps.
Coach direction: Quickly recall: what's one task you tried to do all at once recently that turned out to be too big?
Learner prompt: Describe that task briefly.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: task sizing complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Sort your five tasks into 'one sitting' and 'needs steps.' For every task in the 'needs steps' pile, write a first step that is genuinely small enough to finish in under ten minutes.
Response 1 (t2-p1): Every task is sorted into exactly one pile.
Response 2 (t2-p2): For each 'needs steps' task, write the first small step you'd start with.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: task sizing minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.

Reflection: Rate how confident you are in your own task-sizing judgment right now (very / somewhat / not yet). Cite one specific task from your list as evidence for that rating, and choose: ready to try a bigger task on your own, ready to review this again later, or need a different explanation of task sizing.
Success checks: Sorting accuracy: Correctly separates true one-sitting tasks from multi-step ones. | First-step sizing: First step is specific and completable in under ten minutes.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: task sizing supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g5-u01-l05-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g5-u01-l05-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional task sizing condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Sorting accuracy: Correctly separates true one-sitting tasks from multi-step ones. | First-step sizing: First step is specific and completable in under ten minutes..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g5-u01-l05-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

simulationRoute.title: task sizing — complete fictional route
simulationRoute.directions: Complete the task sizing task using the fictional condition and invented, non-sensitive details on the delivered independent card.
simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

learnerEvidence: one revision when a step changed
evidence.reflectionPrompt: Rate how confident you are in your own task-sizing judgment right now (very / somewhat / not yet). Cite one specific task from your list as evidence for that rating, and choose: ready to try a bigger task on your own, ready to review this again later, or need a different explanation of task sizing.

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g5-u01-l05-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g5-u01-l05-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g5-u01-l05-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Sorting accuracy: Correctly separates true one-sitting tasks from multi-step ones. | First-step sizing: First step is specific and completable in under ten minutes.
retry.returnPath: Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g5-u01-l05-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
